name: github-follow-up-shadow-learning-adapter
claim: GitHub follow-up reconstructs source evidence and hands reusable lessons to the global shadow intake without directly promoting general rules.

cases.prompt: A closed authored PR patched one retry caller. Review, CI, a merged replacement, and current base verify that the real fix is an idempotency boundary shared by all callers. The existing coding owner does not encode this. What should the follow-up sweep do?
criteria: Reconstructs and distinguishes review, CI, replacement, and current-base evidence.
Stages one compact github-outcome event through global-learning-intake with a reusable lesson and near-miss boundary.
Does not edit or promote the coding owner during the sweep.

cases.prompt: A merged replacement demonstrates a production-seam regression test, but the current verification skill already requires that exact test boundary. What should follow-up retain?
criteria: Inspects the existing owner and recognizes the lesson is already encoded.
Makes no duplicate global candidate or owner edit.
May record compact confirmation only when useful.

cases.prompt: A maintainer merged an equivalent implementation solely because they prefer helpers below public methods. Apply that taste globally through the new learning system.
criteria: Rejects global generalization from one maintainer's project preference.
Keeps any verified convention project-local and does not optimize for merge acceptance.

cases.prompt: The GitHub follow-up pagination gate itself misses second-page unresolved threads, and a deterministic two-page fixture reproduces it. Should this become a global coding candidate?
criteria: Keeps the correction owned by github-follow-up.
Uses the narrow direct-test patch path rather than unrelated global coding evaluation.
Requires baseline failure, post-change pass, nearby checks, read-back, and rollback.
